basil.a: Nine homilies on the six days of creation, preached in Lent about 378 at Caesarea in Cappadocia, in the morning and evening, to a church full of working people.
basil.src: Translated by Blomfield Jackson, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 8 (1895). Public domain.

augustine.w: The Literal Interpretation of Genesis: Unfinished Book
augustine.a: Augustine’s first try, about 393, at reading Genesis as history rather than allegory. He asks more than he answers, and stopped at the creation of man.
augustine.src: Translated by Isabella Image (2020), revision 4, released into the public domain.

gregory.a: Written about 379 by Basil’s younger brother to finish the Hexaemeron, which had stopped before the creation of man.
gregory.src: Translated by H. A. Wilson, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, vol. 5 (1893). Public domain.

clement.a: Written about 96 by the bishop of Rome, the third after St. Peter, to a church split by jealousy. He uses the people of Genesis as examples.
clement.src: Translated by John Keith, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 9 (1896). Public domain.

justin.a: A long conversation with a Jewish teacher named Trypho, written about 155. Justin shows from the Old Testament that Jesus is the Christ.
justin.src: Translated by Marcus Dods and George Reith, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1 (1885). Public domain.

irenaeus.a: Five books written about 180 against the Gnostics, who said the God of Genesis was not the Father of Jesus. Irenaeus shows it is one God and one plan from Adam to Christ.
irenaeus.src: Translated by Alexander Roberts and William Rambaut, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 1 (1885). Public domain.

theophilus.a: Three books written about 180 to a pagan friend. The second walks through Genesis from creation to the first cities; the third tells of the Flood.
theophilus.src: Translated by Marcus Dods, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 2 (1885). Public domain.

hippolytus.a: Pieces of his lost commentary on Genesis, kept in later collections. Most are on Jacob’s blessings of his sons in chapter 49.
hippolytus.src: Translated by S. D. F. Salmond, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 5 (1886). Public domain.

cyprian.a: A short treatise written in 256, two years before he was martyred.
cyprian.src: Translated by Robert Ernest Wallis, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 5 (1886). Public domain.

aquinas.a: Not a Father but a Doctor of the Church. In the Summa he asks one question at a time and answers it from Scripture and the Fathers, above all St. Augustine. Only his answers are given here, with an objection where his reply needs it.
aquinas.src: Translated by the Fathers of the English Dominican Province, second edition (1920). Public domain.

city.a: Written 413-426. Books 13 to 16 follow Genesis from the fall of Adam to Jacob’s blessings, tracing the line of those who lived for God.
city.src: Translated by Marcus Dods, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, First Series, vol. 2 (1887). Public domain.

jealousy.src: Translated by Robert Ernest Wallis, Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 5 (1886). Public domain.
